I'm not a particularly emotional person...only two songs have ever actually brought me to tears:

Pink Floyd - "Echoes"

Pink Floyd - "Summer '68"

Not necessarily in that order.

Summer '68 tells the story of a man who, after sleeping with a groupie, reflects on the total lack of emotional satisfaction he got from it. The latter half of the song moves into his dreams for finding satisfaction in life, and how he doesn't have any now. Also, trumpets.

Echoes is a bit more complex. It's a 23-minute-long epic with only three verses - it tells the story of someone who once had love/happiness but didn't appreciate/realize it, lost it, and then later on in life realizes what he lost. It tells this story mostly through music rather than words (the lyrics "bookend" the song, offering only an introduction and conclusion). Most of the song is up for interpretation though - the lack of many lyrics (and the fact that only a verse and a half actually reference any specific "person") means that what the music really means is different from person to person. Took me thirty years to realize what it was trying to say.

I can relate to a lot of songs, I've been moved by quite a few (King Crimson's "Starless" brought me close...) but only these two songs have ever actually made me cry.

From the time we hit kindergarten, we're asked what we want to be when we grow up. When we're small, it's cool stuff like ASTRONAUT! Or PILOT! Or DOLPHIN! Then real life sets in and we realize we're really not certain what we want to be...or even who we really are. If you're like me, you grew up with a few talents but not anything you love enough to do for a living. Maybe you like the idea of traveling but have never been able to do it, yet. Maybe you don't care what you do for a job as long as there's open water somewhere close or a mountain to hike. Maybe you want a new life experience and have questions before you dive in. Maybe something else completely!

You might be asking yourself:

  • Who am I?

  • Where do I fit in?

  • What's important to me? I forgot...or never really knew to begin with.

If questions like these and a vague emptiness about your identity are familiar to you, let's talk about it. Life's so nuts and if it goes all flat on you, it's probably just a case of perspective. With so many possible experiences on this one planet alone, there's no way we won't be able to help each other become the best and most authentic versions of ourselves.

All ages welcome. :D
